_comment: Citations that xref_check.py confirms dangle, which are deliberately NOT fixed by the round that found them, each with the track that owns the fix. Keyed `CODE:identifier`, never file:line — see Finding.key for why. Same idiom as state/known-record-gaps.json: keep a recurring check usable while a real backlog stays open, so that a NEW dangling citation still turns the check red on the round that introduces it. Reasons deliberately carry no per-site COUNTS: a count here would be one more number no round re-executes, the exact rot class this checker exists to catch. Remove an entry the moment its registry is populated; `xref_check.py --show-acknowledged` prints every site an entry is covering. Round 346 REMOVED X002:D-013 after restoring CLAUDE.md's rule sections from commit ee30654 — the entry's own reason ('the body predates this repo's git history') was false, which is why `xref_check.py --provenance` now exists: it asks git whether a dangling id was ever defined, so a repairable gap is never again filed as authorship.

citations.X001:27: language(C). SPEC.md's `## Anti-mainstream design decisions` list ends at 13; round 338 minted `decision 27` and defined it only in a state/research-state.md round entry. Fix = append 27 to the SPEC list, transcribing the definition that already exists; not done by round 345 because writing another track's design rationale is not corpus repair.
citations.X001:28: language(C). Round 342 (v0.18) minted `decision 28`, defined only in a state/research-state.md round entry. Same fix, same reason as X001:27.
citations.X001:29: language(C). Round 344 minted `decision 29` for v0.19 parameter contracts and was killed by the driver's 3300s timeout before writing SPEC at all, so 29 is defined NOWHERE. Round 345 landed round 344's code (commit 6132f1f) and left the SPEC section to the track that owns it.
